To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ICZM in China is not a top-down but a bottom-up process.

(1) ICZM as a framework is generally accepted in China; (2) ICZM has been implemented in some coastal cities; (3) ICZM is a top-down process in China, but bottom-up implementation is possible; (4) The political system is an obstacle to ICZM in China.
ICZM in China has to face a number of structural constraints.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the institutional framework of decision-making and its power distribution in China affects the implementation of ICZM.
the question of how ICZM could be introduced to China.
the question of how ICZM can be introduced in the Chinese political context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the implementation of ICZM in China is not only a question of content, but also of structural issues.
the ICZM concept is not suitable for implementation in China.
the implementation of ICZM in China is a very difficult and complex task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the political system is the most important factor influencing ICZM implementation in China.
the political system in the PRC is a main constraint in the implementation of ICZM.
the ICZM approach is a good concept but that it is not a magic bullet that can be used to solve all coastal management problems in a uniform manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the political system in the PRC constrains the implementation of ICZM.
the political structures in China are not a constraint to ICZM, but that the political system is an integral part of the approach.
a successful implementation of ICZM requires a thorough analysis of the political and social structures within which the implementation is to take place.
